narrative: A large feature PR (document variables, parse seam) took five reviewed rounds plus a cap-hit sixth, and 19 of 40 findings were caused by earlier fixes. The costliest chain began with a test-leak finding (F20): the agent widened it into process-group and AbortSignal semantics for the shared launch() primitive, which produced a rethrow from timers (F29), then a promise-rejection contract break (F30/F33), then comment and type-scope findings (F34, F37, F38). A second chain came from naming a fix commit for F15 that depended on an unpublished go-template-js release, so the same dependency gap was re-raised three times (F18, F25, F27). Every round also had at least one finding on original code, so no round was strictly avoidable; most of the agent's choices to accept, push back, or take a different fix were sound.
guidance_observations: Fixes to a shared primitive (launch.ts) were made one finding at a time without sweeping callers and sibling functions, so each contract change surfaced as its own later round.
The agent replied 'Fixed in <sha>' for a change that could not compile against the locked dependency, which invited re-raises in two later rounds.
Several fixes corrected one instance (a comment, a CRLF split, a missing test) without grepping for the same claim or pattern elsewhere (CLAUDE.md, the parsers, the formatter's tests).
Many round 1 to 4 flags were false positives on code that predated review, so the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag over-counts fix-caused findings for multi-commit PRs.
